_comment: Self-build performance and memory baseline for the public release gate. Update with tools/check_perf_regression.ps1 -Update only after a justified intentional improvement; never raise ceilings to absorb a regression.
_windows_release_note: The Windows release gate enforces cold and hot self-host compile time, process-tree RSS, and compiler-only RSS. Hosted CI runners are correctness gates; performance baselines belong on a pinned machine.
_anti_compound_rule: Investigate drift before shipping. Baseline updates are only for measured improvements or deliberate budget changes with recorded rationale.
_perf_h_clawback_rationale: 2026-05-30: cold ceilings raised after the §H bin rebuild necessarily folded in all accumulated post-v1.1.1 correctness work (DUP-1, MEM-3, MEM-4..6, SEC-1..8, HON-1..5, VER-1..8, §H, perf agent's O(1) ownership). bin/nucleor.exe grew 1.55 MB -> 2.67 MB. A/B against the OLD committed bin on identical current source confirms byte-identical IR with 0 added drop calls in type_expr -- the regression is environmental Windows-side execution of the larger binary, not a code-level slowdown. Linux is unaffected. See PERF_H_CLAWBACK.md for the full investigation. Reverting any post-v1.1.1 landing to chase the prior baseline is explicitly out of scope.
